text.p: Poland's prime minister dismissed police chief Jerzy Stanczyk from his post on Friday, the national police spokesman said.
Stanczyk, who in March 1995 assumed the post as Poland's fourth police chief since the 1989 fall of communism, had announced last month that he planned to resign.
"The Premier removed him today from his post," spokesman Andrzej Przemyski said. He said he could not give further details or the name of Stanczyk's successor.
PAP said Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz also dismissed the head of the border guard service, Jan Wojcieszczuk, who had held the post since 1992.
Last year Stanczyk suffered a personal tragedy when his daughter died after being found unconscious with head wounds in a street near her home in the German city of Hamburg.

During his time at the helm, the government claimed successes in combatting several kinds of crime, including car theft, assault and burglary -- all of which had grown since the collapse of the old communist order.
